messages.subject: nei's population distance
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to get a distance tree based off population, not individual. I've been successful in following the tutorial doing the individuals, but need to look at populations. The issue I'm getting is when I try to make strata. 

I run this code:

strata(d) <- data.frame(other(d))

and get this error:

Error: Number of rows in data frame not equal to number of individuals in object.

I've followed and altered my genalex file the best I could based off of your examples in the tutorials, and can't find any differences. Any ways to help out? 

Thank you,
Alex

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: nei's population distance
parts:
Hi Alex,


From what you've provided, I can surmise that "d" is a genind or genclone object containing data for individuals (you would get a completely different error, otherwise). The code you've provided me looks like you are trying to convert whatever is in the "other" slot into a data frame and use that for the strata (this would only work if all elements in the "other" slot are the same size as your data). 


You can get the same error with the following code:


library(adegenet)
data(nancycats)
strata(nancycats) <- data.frame(other(nancycats))

## Error: Number of rows in data frame not equal to number of individuals in object.


You can see why this failed if you looked at the number of rows in the data frame you're using to define your strata:


nrow(data.frame(other(nancycats)))

## [1] 17

nInd(nancycats)

## [1] 237

It's possible that you don't have anything in the "other" slot, which would give you the same error.


I've written a small tutorial about dealing with strata here: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/blob/master/tutorials/tutorial-strata.pdf
You have two options to use strata (detailed in the tutorial):

1. Import a data frame of strata defined for each sample from a separate file with read.table() and then use strata() as you did above.
2. Define your strata in the population column in your import file and then use splitStrata() to split up the different strata into columns.

After that, you can use genind2genpop to convert to a genpop object using any definition of strata and then use aboot to bootstrap.

I hope that helps. Let me know if you have any further questions.

Zhian
